_note: Extension to the curated skills.json that adds hard_guard rules learned from c2hls matrix sweeps. Always retrieved alongside the base skills; never filtered out.

skills.pattern: the kernel contains a floating-point reduction such as `acc += a[i] * b[i]`, `tmp[i][j] += alpha * A[i][k] * B[k][j]`, or similar serial accumulator, AND the testbench compares output bit-for-bit (no fabs/epsilon tolerance check)
skills.strategy: DO NOT unroll, partial-unroll, or reorder a serial floating-point accumulator. IEEE 754 + and * are not associative, so any reassociation changes the bit-exact result and breaks csim. If the testbench does NOT have an explicit tolerance check (fabs(a-b) < EPSILON), the only safe options are: (1) keep the reduction serial and pipeline its body, or (2) use a tree reduction with explicit ordering that mathematically matches the serial one (rarely possible without algorithmic insight). Lane-parallel partial sums are NOT safe unless the testbench tolerates non-bit-exact output.
required_steps: scan the kernel for accumulation patterns: `acc +=`, `tmp += alpha * x`, `result[i][j] += ...`
scan the testbench for tolerance checks: `fabs(`, `EPSILON`, `< 1e-6`, `relative_error`
if testbench is bit-exact and a reduction is found: do NOT apply UNROLL on the inner loop containing the accumulator
do NOT apply ARRAY_PARTITION complete on accumulator arrays
for the reduction loop, keep II=N where N is the FP add latency (typically 5-9 cycles), not II=1
if a higher-priority optimization skill (coalescing, lane-parallel) would touch a reduction loop, DEFER to this guard and skip the loop
guards: this is a hard_guard — applies before any other transformation skill
floating-point + and * are NOT associative under IEEE 754
bit-exact csim fails on ANY reassociation of FP reduction
polybench, machsuite, and most HLS testbenches use bit-exact dumps (no tolerance)
the c2hls matrix sweep on 2026-05-24 confirmed 3/3 csim failures in haiku multistep skills=on on reduction-heavy kernels (gemm, gemver, syrk) came from this exact violation

skills.pattern: the most recent synthesis report shows resource usage already above 50% of any Artix-7 100T device limit (BRAM>135, DSP>120, FF>63400, LUT>31700) — i.e. an additional parallelism-increasing transform risks busting the budget
skills.strategy: Refined to be state-aware (2026-05-25): this guard fires only when an actual synth report shows resource pressure, not blanket at translation time. The c2hls rubric scores Device Feasibility on Artix-7 100T limits (BRAM 270, DSP 240, FF 126800, LUT 63400). When the current report shows you're already past 50% of any limit, BACK OFF further parallelism: reduce UNROLL factors, switch ARRAY_PARTITION complete → cyclic factor=4/8, prefer rolling buffers over full ping-pong. When the report is well within budget, this skill should NOT be retrieved — normal optimization may proceed.
required_steps: before applying UNROLL: estimate per-iteration FP ops × unroll_factor ≤ 240 DSP
before applying ARRAY_PARTITION complete on dim=1: estimate element_count × element_bitwidth ≤ 126800 FF; if larger, use cyclic factor=4 or factor=8 instead
for an N×M matrix array, complete partitioning yields N×M registers — only safe if N×M < 1000
for double-precision FP, each mul is ~3 DSP and each add is ~2 DSP under default Vitis 2023.2 schedule
for a kernel with K nested FP multiply-adds and outer unroll factor U, expect roughly U * (K * 5) DSP — keep U * K * 5 < 240 (i.e. U * K < 48)
if the gold baseline used 0 BRAM and your design uses > 100 BRAM, you almost certainly introduced superficial tiling — back it out
guards: this is a conditional_guard — only retrieved when current synth report shows >50% of any device-limit
the c2hls rubric weights Feasibility at 10% and Resources at 17% — busting limits forfeits ~27% of total score
the Vitis estimator is conservative — actual usage may be 1.2-1.5x the post-synth estimate

previous 'always-on' version of this guard was too blunt: it suppressed parallelism even on benches with plenty of headroom (nussinov -20pt, bicg -13pt). State-aware version only restrains when there's evidence of pressure
do NOT apply this guard preemptively at translation time — wait for the first synth report

skills.pattern: a loop has a bound that is a function argument, struct field, or any non-compile-time constant, and Vitis HLS cannot determine the trip count
skills.strategy: Annotate any non-compile-time-bounded loop with `#pragma HLS loop_tripcount min=N avg=N max=N` so the synthesis report has a numeric latency estimate. Without this, latency comes back as 'undef' and the c2hls rubric scores 0 on M4 (Latency, 23% of total). On polybench kernels the upper bounds are tiny (40-100), so this is essentially free.
required_steps: scan the kernel for loops with non-constant bounds: `for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i)` where n is a parameter
for each such loop, find the actual maximum value (usually defined as a macro or constant in the header)
add `#pragma HLS loop_tripcount min=N avg=N max=N` immediately after the loop opening brace
use the max as a conservative estimate; the rubric scores based on the reported number
guards: loop_tripcount does NOT affect functional correctness — it only annotates for the scheduler/reporter
providing a tripcount that's smaller than the actual runtime trip count is safe (estimate vs actual)
if the loop runs at most N times statically, ALWAYS annotate it
